name: Lemon-Garlic Steak Bites with Mushrooms & Tallow Potatoes
ingredients:
1.5 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in 1-inch chunks
1/2 tsp baking soda
1 tbsp beef tallow
1.25 lb top sirloin, trimmed, cut in 1-inch cubes
8 oz pre-sliced cremini mushrooms
2 tsp dried minced garlic (for the beef)
1/2 tsp dried minced garlic (for the potatoes)
1 lemon, zested and juiced
1 tbsp avocado oil, divided
1.5 tsp salt, plus more for the potato water
3/4 tsp black pepper
directions:
Soak garlic: Stir the dried minced garlic for the beef into the lemon juice and set aside to rehydrate while you cook.
Parboil potatoes: Place potatoes in a pot of cold, well-salted water with the baking soda. Bring to a boil and cook 6–8 minutes, until a knife slides in but they hold their shape.
Season beef: While the potatoes boil, pat the sirloin dry and season with half the salt and all the pepper.
Drain and rough up: Drain the potatoes and let them steam-dry for 2 minutes. Shake the colander hard to rough up the edges.
Crisp potatoes: Heat the tallow in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add potatoes in one layer and leave untouched 4–5 minutes, until deep golden underneath and they release on their own. Flip and repeat, about 12–15 minutes total. Keep them going while you cook the mushrooms and beef.
Brown mushrooms: In a second large skillet over medium-high, add half the avocado oil, then the mushrooms with a pinch of salt. Leave untouched 3 minutes, then stir and cook 3–4 minutes more, until browned and the liquid has cooked off. Transfer to a plate.
Sear beef: Turn the second skillet to high. Add the remaining avocado oil and the beef in a single layer. Sear 1–2 minutes per side until browned outside and pink inside.
Garlic and lemon: Lower the heat. Add the soaked garlic with its lemon juice, the mushrooms, and most of the lemon zest. Toss about 30 seconds.
Finish potatoes and serve: Toss the potatoes with the remaining salt, the dried minced garlic for the potatoes, and the remaining lemon zest for the last 30 seconds. Serve alongside the steak and mushrooms.
notes:
Roughly 33g protein and 12g fat per serving.
Dried minced garlic burns in seconds in hot fat; rehydrating it in the lemon juice prevents bitterness. To use fresh garlic instead, substitute 5 minced cloves and add them straight to the pan.
The baking soda roughs up the potato surfaces for a crunchier crust. Parboiled potatoes are soft, so handle gently and don't flip until they release.
Cook the mushrooms before the beef so their liquid doesn't steam the steak. Pat the beef dry and never crowd either pan.
